messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: multi-region failover detected — elevated 5xx errors and latency across customer-facing endpoints. Patchy traffic shift from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 observed. Paging @oncall. Severity: P1. Impact: ~25% request error rate for some customers in NA.

Alex (oncall): ack, I'm on it. Gathering initial context. @Sam can you pull the healthcheck logs and route metrics?

Sam: looking now. Quick heads-up — Route53 healthchecks for origin-us-east are flapping, CloudWatch shows multiple Origin 502 spikes starting ~2024-09-12T03:12Z.

Maria N: seeing BGP withdraws for a subset of AZs in us-east-1 (likely AZa). AS path changes and some routes briefly moved to us-west-2. Could be a provider edge issue.

Alex (oncall): good catch. Is traffic shifting because our regional edge is marking endpoints unhealthy or because provider is withdrawing routes?

Maria N: initial packet captures show RSTs toward a set of instances in AZa, then edge LB healthchecks fail. Provider control plane events around 03:10Z in us-east-1 per provider status feed.

DevOps Bot: deploybot: No recent deploys to production in the last 2 hours.

Sam: pulling ELB logs and ALB target group health: a subset of targets in us-east-1/az-a are showing 502 and connection reset. Rest of us-east targets OK.

Alex (oncall): mitigation options: 1) drain problematic AZ (az-a) manually at the LB level, force rebalancing; 2) fail traffic back to healthy endpoints in us-east/b and us-west with weighted routing; 3) engage cloud provider for underlying network flaps.

Priya: I'm the oncall-2 in 30m, but available to help now. Recommend we start with draining AZa and enabling increased capacity in us-west to absorb shift.

Alex (oncall): executing step 1: marking targets in us-east-1a unhealthy in ALB -> `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <tg-arn> --targets Id=i-0abcd...` (run with careful tagging).

Sam: logs show gradual error rate drop after we started deregistering. Latency improving for requests routed to us-west. However some customers still see 502s due to cached upstream routes.

Maria N: opened ticket with provider (ticket #PROV-9342). They report partial edge fabric instability in the AZ. They're investigating.

Alex (oncall): status page update: adding note "Partial degradation in us-east-1 affecting some customers; mitigation in progress; traffic shifting to alternate region." Priya, can you take over detailed comms if I need to step out?

Priya: happy to own customer comms. I'll prepare an impact blurb and contact top customers via CSMs.

DevOps Bot: autoscale triggered in us-west-2 — 4 extra instances launched to maintain capacity.

Sam: confirm: 502s down from 25% -> 8% over the last 10 minutes. Error budget still at risk for some SLOs.

Alex (oncall): call with provider scheduled at 03:35Z. For now continue draining and keep weighted routing to healthy endpoints. Also enable additional caching layer for static assets to reduce request pressure.

Maria N: Provider indicates a partial misconfiguration in their internal load balancer for AZa that caused healthcheck timeouts. They have engineers patching now. ETA unknown.

Sam: performing targeted retry/backoff for failed requests at edge — `circuit-breaker: short-circuit` toggled to reduce retries that amplify errors.

Alex (oncall): note for incident doc: root cause suspected provider AZ edge fabric instability leading to unhealthy target reports triggering cross-region failover. Secondary factors: aggressive healthcheck behavior and lack of per-AZ graceful draining.

Priya: preparing customer impact summary: - Affected customers: subset in NA (estimated 12 accounts saw errors) - Impact: intermittent 502s and elevated latency between 03:10Z-03:45Z - Mitigation: isolated AZa, traffic rebalanced to us-east-1b and us-west-2, provider engaged - Next steps: postmortem + retries on SDKs to better handle transient cross-region failovers.

Alex (oncall): handoff: I'm stepping off for a brief break. @Priya you're the incident lead moving forward. I'll be available on DM if needed.

Priya: taking lead. Logging playbook steps in incident doc. Can someone confirm we've captured start/end times and affected customer IDs?

Sam: pulled a list of affected customer IDs and added to the incident doc (masked IDs): cust-****1, cust-****9, cust-****2. I'll attach logs to the internal postmortem.

status-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATED: partial degradation in us-east-1, mitigation in progress.

Maria N: provider confirms fix rolled to edge LB for AZa at 03:40Z and routes gradually restored. We're watching healthchecks.

Sam: ALB targets in us-east-1a back to healthy at 03:52Z. Traffic is shifting back, and global error rate normalized by ~03:55Z.

Priya: final impact note for customers: disruption window ~03:10Z–03:55Z; intermittent 5xx and latency for a subset. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and action items.

Alex (oncall): closing actions: - Postmortem assigned to Alex + Maria + Sam + Priya - Improve per-AZ healthcheck backoff to avoid aggressive cross-region failover - Add playbook automation to drain an AZ and throttle routing weight instead of full failover - Follow up with cloud provider for SLA credit review.

Priya: creating incident ticket in tracker and assigning follow-ups. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: P1 downgraded to P2. Root cause: provider edge fabric instability; mitigations applied and traffic normalized.
